about: Stella's owner-facing alert codes (D44). bin/alert.sh renders #alerts messages from this file; bin/alert-catalog.sh --docs writes docs/alert-codes.md from it. A code is never reused or renumbered: retire one with "status": "retired". Placeholders: {name}, filled from the caller's key=value pairs; {since} and {now} are times, shown in the owner's time zone; {what} is the plain phrase for the caller's error=.

alerts.title: self-check is failing
alerts.message: The automatic {check} failed on the latest version of the stack (commit {commit}).{detail} Stella keeps running, but one of her own checks no longer passes.
alerts.action: ask Stella to run the tests. Nothing else is needed from you right now.
alerts.cause: A recent change broke a test, the code style check (lint) or the build; or a test depends on something outside the container that changed. A test that fails once is run again on its own first, so only a test that fails twice in a row raises this alert.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log (full test output, and a line `flaky:` for a test that failed once and passed on the rerun); .supervisor/status.json (which step, exit code); `npm test` in the container.
alerts.resolved_message: The automatic checks pass again on commit {commit}. They were failing from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: self-check got stuck
alerts.message: The automatic {check} did not finish in time and was stopped (commit {commit}). Stella keeps running, but her own checks cannot complete.
alerts.action: ask Stella to run the tests and find the one that hangs.
alerts.cause: A test waits forever (a network call, a lock, a prompt for input), or the container is badly overloaded. The step is killed after WATCHDOG_STEP_TIMEOUT (600 s).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log (output up to the kill); .supervisor/status.json ("hung": true).
alerts.resolved_message: The automatic checks finish and pass again on commit {commit}. They were stuck from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: Stella's program is not running
alerts.message: No running program for Stella's chat connection was found, and she was not paused on purpose. She cannot see or answer messages until it runs again.
alerts.action: run the Windows recovery script, or ask your coding agent to restart Stella (see STL-GW-101 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The gateway process crashed or was stopped, or the container restarted without starting it. The check is a process lookup, so it says nothing about the chat connection itself.
alerts.check: docs/recovery.md; `tmux ls` and `hermes status` in the container; ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log.
alerts.resolved_message: Stella's chat program is running again. It was reported as not running from {since} to {now}; at {now} the check saw: {parts}.

parts.quiet: her program is running and the newest connection line in her log says connected; nothing was written for a while, which is normal when nobody writes to her
parts.settings: the settings for this check are missing or invalid
parts.process_check: the check could not look for her program
parts.logs: her log files cannot be read
parts.no_marker: her program is running, but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour
parts.check: the check itself did not run
parts._other: something the check could not name

alerts.title: Stella lost her chat connection
alerts.message: Stella's log shows her chat connection dropped at {at} and has not come back since. Her program is still running and keeps retrying, but she may not see or answer messages until it connects.
alerts.action: wait a few minutes: she usually reconnects by herself, and a ✅ message follows. If it does not, send her a message in the chat, and if she does not answer ask your coding agent to restart her (see STL-GW-102 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The chat platform or the container's network dropped the connection and the reconnect attempts keep failing (DNS, network, a platform outage, revoked access). The check reads the newest connection line in her log; it is not a live test, and a quiet log alone never raises this.
alerts.check: ~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log (the last `[Discord] Disconnected` / `Reconnect` lines); `bin/watchdog_settings.py gateway` (the verdict and its evidence); `hermes status`; docs/recovery.md.
alerts.resolved_message: Stella's chat connection looks healthy again. The loss was reported from {since} to {now}; at {now} the check saw: {parts}.

parts.quiet: her program is running and the newest connection line in her log says connected; nothing was written for a while, which is normal when nobody writes to her
parts.settings: the settings for this check are missing or invalid
parts.process_check: the check could not look for her program
parts.logs: her log files cannot be read
parts.no_marker: her program is running, but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour
parts.check: the check itself did not run
parts._other: something the check could not name

alerts.title: can't tell if Stella is connected
alerts.message: The automatic check could not find out whether Stella's chat connection works: {parts}. This alone does not prove that Stella is down.
alerts.action: ask your coding agent to look at the watchdog (see STL-GW-103 in docs/alert-codes.md). Nothing else is needed from you right now.
alerts.cause: The watchdog settings file is missing or invalid, the process lookup could not run, the log files cannot be read, or Stella's program runs but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour.
alerts.check: `bin/watchdog_settings.py --check`; `bin/watchdog_settings.py gateway` (the verdict and its evidence); .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log.
alerts.resolved_message: The check can tell again whether Stella is connected. It could not tell from {since} to {now}; at {now} it saw: {parts}.

parts.quiet: her program is running and the newest connection line in her log says connected; nothing was written for a while, which is normal when nobody writes to her
parts.settings: the settings for this check are missing or invalid
parts.process_check: the check could not look for her program
parts.logs: her log files cannot be read
parts.no_marker: her program is running, but her log shows no connection line and nothing new for an hour
parts.check: the check itself did not run
parts._other: something the check could not name
parts.state_stale: her program is running and her log says connected, but she stopped updating her own status, so she may be stuck

alerts.title: not watching for your replies
alerts.message: The part of Stella that reads your replies in escalation threads has not run for {minutes} minutes. Your replies are not picked up, and finished cards are not reported, until it runs again.
alerts.action: it usually starts again by itself. If it is still here after 15 minutes, ask your coding agent to check the reply checker (see STL-ESC-201 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The container's scheduled jobs (cron) stopped, the container restarted, or bin/escalation-reply-poll.sh is stuck or failing at start.
alerts.check: .supervisor/state/reply-poll.heartbeat (time of the last run); `crontab -l`; run bin/escalation-reply-poll.sh by hand and read its output.
alerts.resolved_message: The part of Stella that reads your replies runs again. The check saw no run from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: can't read replies in an escalation thread
alerts.message: Stella tried {count} times in a row and could not read the thread for card {card} ({what}). Replies there are not being seen until this clears.
alerts.action: it usually clears when the connection recovers. If it is still here after an hour, see STL-ESC-210 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Network or DNS trouble, a dropped secure connection, a platform outage or rate limit, the thread was deleted by hand, or the bot lost access to #escalations. A short platform or network drop (a minute or two) is the usual case: the alert needs only 3 failed reads in a row, and Stella keeps reading every few seconds.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log and .supervisor/escalations.log (POLL_FAIL lines hold the raw error and the thread id); `bin/owner-config.sh --verify`.
alerts.resolved_title: replies in an escalation thread are read again
alerts.resolved_message: Stella can read the thread for card {card} again. It could not from {since} to {now}; replies posted meanwhile are picked up now.

alerts.title: can't read the task board
alerts.message: Stella could not read her task board, so your replies and finished cards are not being processed until it works again.
alerts.action: nothing yet, Stella will retry every minute. If it is still here after an hour, ask your coding agent to check the board (see STL-ESC-211 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The kanban database is locked or damaged, the ~/.hermes volume is full or unreadable, or the hermes command is missing from the job's PATH.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (POLL_FAIL "kanban list failed"); `hermes kanban list` in the container.

alerts.title: couldn't pass your reply on to its card
alerts.message: Your reply for card {card} was seen, but Stella could not pass it on to the card. She tries again every minute.
alerts.action: nothing, Stella will retry. If it is still here after an hour, see STL-ESC-212 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The kanban unblock call failed: the card changed state meanwhile, the board is locked, or the hermes command failed.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (UNBLOCK_FAIL for the card); `hermes kanban show <card>`.

alerts.title: an escalation was not posted
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") needs a decision from you, but Stella could not post it in #escalations ({what}). The card stays blocked.
alerts.action: nothing yet, Stella tries again up to 3 times over the next 20 minutes. The question is also on the card itself.
alerts.cause: The chat platform was unreachable or refused the request, the #escalations channel id in the owner settings is wrong, or another run held the card's lock.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log and .supervisor/escalations.log (THREAD_FAIL with the raw error); `bin/owner-config.sh --verify`.

alerts.title: an escalation could not be posted after 3 tries
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") needs a decision from you, but Stella could not post it in #escalations after 3 tries. She has stopped trying, and the card stays blocked.
alerts.action: ask Stella to look at card {card} and post its escalation again (see STL-ESC-221 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The same causes as STL-ESC-220, lasting over 20 minutes.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (THREAD_FAIL and THREAD_RETRY for the card); .supervisor/state/thread-retry.tsv; `bin/escalation-thread.sh --check`.

alerts.title: escalation notice missing in #supervisor
alerts.message: The question for card {card} was posted in its escalation thread, but the notice in #supervisor could not be posted ({what}). You will not see it there.
alerts.action: open #escalations, find the thread for card {card}, and reply there as usual.
alerts.cause: The #supervisor channel id in the owner settings is wrong, the bot lost access to #supervisor, or the chat platform was unreachable.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (LINK_FAIL with the raw error); `bin/owner-config.sh --verify`.

alerts.title: a card is stuck in a loop
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") was blocked again after you already answered twice ({count} blocks so far). Stella has stopped asking you and holds it for a closer look.
alerts.action: ask Stella to look at card {card}; your replies no longer unblock it on their own.
alerts.cause: The worker does not act on the answer (a misread reply, a missing ability, or the card asks for something impossible).
alerts.check: the card's comments (`hermes kanban show <card>`); .supervisor/escalations.log (LOOP_HELD).

alerts.title: a card's builder can't do it
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") stopped because its builder hit something it cannot do (a missing tool, access or skill). This is not a question for you, so no escalation thread was opened.
alerts.action: read the comment on card {card}, then give it to another builder (the Claude builder can do more) or change the card.
alerts.cause: The builder's tools or model cannot do the task; the exact error is in the card comment.
alerts.check: the card's comment "Capability block held for triage" (`hermes kanban show <card>`); .supervisor/escalations.log (CAPABILITY_HELD).

alerts.title: ignored a reply from someone else
alerts.message: Someone who is not the configured owner replied in the escalation thread for card {card}. The reply was not applied. If that was you, your Discord user id in the owner settings is wrong.
alerts.action: if it was you, correct your Discord user id in the owner settings; STL-ESC-240 in docs/alert-codes.md says how. The reply is then applied within a minute.
alerts.cause: OWNER_DISCORD_USER_ID in config/owner.env is not your id, or another member of the server replied.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (REPLY_IGNORED_NOT_OWNER with the author id); to fix: `chmod u+w config config/owner.env`, edit it, then `chmod 555 config; chmod 444 config/owner.env` (from Windows, just edit it).

alerts.title: owner settings are missing or unreadable
alerts.message: Stella cannot read the owner settings, so escalations are stopped: no new threads are opened and replies are not applied.{fix}
alerts.action: correct the owner settings (the example file shows every accepted form) or recreate them from it; STL-CFG-301 in docs/alert-codes.md says how.
alerts.cause: config/owner.env is missing (a fresh clone or a deleted file), unreadable, has a malformed line, or lacks a required key.
alerts.check: `bin/owner-config.sh --check` (names the problem); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (raw error); copy config/owner.example.env to config/owner.env and fill it in (docs/recovery.md).

alerts.title: your Discord user id in the settings is not valid
alerts.message: The owner's Discord user id in the settings is empty or not a valid Discord id, so Stella ignores every reply and reaction in the escalation threads until it is fixed. Replies already posted are applied after the fix.
alerts.action: correct your Discord user id in the owner settings; STL-CFG-302 in docs/alert-codes.md says how.
alerts.cause: OWNER_DISCORD_USER_ID in config/owner.env is empty or not 17 to 20 digits (a typo, a username instead of the id, extra characters).
alerts.check: `bin/owner-config.sh --check`; to fix: `chmod u+w config config/owner.env`, edit it, then `chmod 555 config; chmod 444 config/owner.env` (from Windows, just edit it).

alerts.title: a Claude request was held (limit reached)
alerts.message: A request to Claude {model} for card {card} was not sent because one of Stella's usage limits is reached. It is saved and can be sent later.
alerts.action: nothing right now. When the limit resets, ask Stella to send the held requests (see STL-LIM-401 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: All Opus slots are busy (OPUS_MAX_CONCURRENT), or the Haiku daily limit (HAIKU_MAX_PER_DAY) is used up, or a limit is set to 0.
alerts.check: .supervisor/limits.env; `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`; .supervisor/escalations.log (QUEUED, LIMIT).

alerts.title: Claude usage is used up
alerts.message: Claude has no usage left right now, so a {model} request for card {card} was not sent. It is saved and can be sent later.
alerts.action: nothing until the usage resets. Then ask Stella to send the held requests (see STL-LIM-402 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The Claude subscription's session or weekly limit, or the organisation's usage credits, are used up.
alerts.check: `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`; .supervisor/escalations.log (POOL_EXHAUSTED with the matched message).

alerts.title: a Claude request was answered by a fallback model
alerts.message: Claude has no usage left right now, so a {model} request for card {card} was answered by a different, free model ({served}) through the OmniRoute gateway. The answer is labelled as a fallback; it is not a Claude answer.
alerts.action: nothing, unless the card is important: check the fallback answer before relying on it, and send the request to Claude later if it matters (see STL-LIM-404 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The Claude subscription's limit was reached (STL-LIM-402) on a low-risk card and the fallback is switched on (`enabled: true` in docs/hermes-local/fallback-routing.json). High-risk cards are never rerouted. Retired in F2b item E: an escalation rung is never rerouted to the fallback runner (E-DC-07), it is queued (STL-LIM-402).
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (POOL_EXHAUSTED then FALLBACK, with the serving model); the card's comments; the OmniRoute gateway on loopback.

alerts.title: the list of held Claude requests is full
alerts.message: Stella already holds {max} Claude requests that could not be sent. New ones are refused and not saved until the list is cleared.
alerts.action: ask Stella to look at the held requests and send or clear them (see STL-LIM-403 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: Limits or an exhausted usage pool held many requests and nobody sent them (QUEUE_MAX, default 50).
alerts.check: `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`; .supervisor/state/queue.jsonl.

alerts.title: a Claude request was lost (not sent, not saved)
alerts.message: A request to Claude {model} for card {card} was not sent and could not be saved for later: {problem}. It is lost. Later requests that cannot be sent are lost the same way until this is fixed; this alert comes at most once an hour.
alerts.action: fix or move aside the file the message names, then run the lost requests again: .supervisor/escalations.log has one NOT_QUEUED line for each (see STL-LIM-405 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The list of held requests (.supervisor/state/queue.jsonl) cannot be read, parsed or written: a cut or hand-edited line, a permission, or a full disk.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (NOT_QUEUED, one line per lost request); .supervisor/state/queue.jsonl; `bin/escalate-drain.sh --list`.

alerts.title: the usage ledger does not know that link
alerts.message: The usage ledger refused a call or a limit: {problem}. Nothing was recorded or limited for it.
alerts.action: check the connection and model id in the call against `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections`; a link the catalog lacks is added by the owner first. See STL-LIM-410 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A record, status, slot or observation named a connection or a model the catalog (.stella/connections.json) does not have. The ledger fails closed: it never counts a link it cannot find limits for.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/ledger.py status --connection <id> [--model <id>] --json`

alerts.title: a usage record was refused
alerts.message: The usage ledger refused a call record: {problem}. It was not written.
alerts.action: fix the caller so its record has the fields of .stella/schemas/usage.schema.json (tokens are whole numbers, outcome one of ok, error, limit, timeout, refused). See STL-LIM-411 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The record is not JSON, or breaks the usage schema (a negative or fractional token count, an unknown field, a wrong type).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/ledger.py record --json < call.json`; .stella/schemas/usage.schema.json

alerts.title: a link's limit refused a call
alerts.message: A call of a link was refused by its limits: {problem}. It is not an error: the caller waits or takes the next link.
alerts.action: nothing, unless it keeps happening: `python3 bin/ledger.py status --connection <id> --model <id> --json` shows the slots, the daily count and the observed limit with the time each ends. See STL-LIM-412 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: All slots of the link are held (exit 75 of `ledger.py hold`), its daily cap of the UTC day is used (76), or a limit was observed on it and has not expired (77).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/ledger.py status --connection <id> --model <id> --json`; the limit.hit and limit.observed lines of the event log

alerts.title: a ledger file or lock cannot be used
alerts.message: The usage ledger cannot use one of its files: {problem}. Calls that need it are refused until it is fixed.
alerts.action: fix or move aside the file the message names (a slot lock file under the ledger state folder, the usage file, its lock), then run `python3 bin/ledger.py check --json`. See STL-LIM-413 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A file is a symbolic link or has a second hard link (no write goes through it), cannot be written whole, or the folder is not writable.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/ledger.py check --json`; the usage_ledger and ledger_state paths in .stella/data-files.json

alerts.title: the usage ledger files do not check out
alerts.message: The usage ledger's files do not pass their check: {problem}.
alerts.action: fix or move aside the line or file the message names (the usage file is protected state: the owner does it), then run `python3 bin/ledger.py check --json` again. See STL-LIM-414 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A usage line breaks the usage schema or repeats an id, the ledger state file breaks its schema or cannot be read, or the limit-signals data is unusable. A torn last line (a writer killed mid-write) is skipped and only counted.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/ledger.py check --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`

alerts.title: a limit value cannot be read
alerts.message: A limit of a link cannot be read: {problem}. It counts as 0, so the link serves nothing until it is fixed.
alerts.action: set the limit in the catalog to a whole number, or define the limits.env key it names with a whole number. See STL-LIM-415 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A model's or connection's max_concurrent or per_day names a key .supervisor/limits.env does not define, or its value is not a whole number (the same rule as bin/escalate.sh).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/ledger.py status --connection <id> --model <id> --json` (problems); .supervisor/limits.env

alerts.title: Stella's settings were not applied at start
alerts.message: When the container started, Stella's settings and safety guards could not be fully applied. She runs, but some guards may be missing.
alerts.action: ask your coding agent to apply Stella's settings again and read the output.
alerts.cause: bin/apply-hermes-local.sh failed at container start: owner settings missing, a SOUL placeholder error, or the ~/.hermes volume unreadable.
alerts.check: run bin/apply-hermes-local.sh in the container and read its output; .supervisor/logs (container start).
alerts.related: D44; bin/container-start.sh (still sends its own text: a reboot-relevant file, not converted)

alerts.title: Stella was restarted by the recovery script
alerts.message: At {now} the Windows recovery script found part of Stella not running and started it again: {restarted}. Her last healthy check was at {last_ok}.
alerts.action: nothing, Stella is running again.
alerts.cause: Windows rebooted or slept, Docker Desktop stopped, or the container or its gateway session died.
alerts.check: the recovery log on Windows (docs/recovery.md); `hermes status` in the container.

alerts.title: Stella was restarted, but something still fails
alerts.message: At {now} the Windows recovery script found part of Stella not running and started it again: {restarted}. Her last healthy check was at {last_ok}. Still not working: {failing}.
alerts.action: run the Windows recovery script again; if it still fails, see STL-RCV-503 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: One recovery step failed (often the local model server, Ollama, or the firewall step) while the rest came back.
alerts.check: the recovery log on Windows (docs/recovery.md); `hermes status` in the container.

alerts.title: Stella's network protection is incomplete
alerts.message: The Windows recovery script restarted or repaired something, but the internet restrictions she runs under are not fully in place, even after they were applied again. Found: {parts}.
alerts.action: ask your coding agent to check and repair the network protection (see STL-RCV-504 in docs/alert-codes.md). This message is sent at most once every 6 hours for the same problem.
alerts.cause: init-firewall.sh did not build the full ruleset (the container image is older than the current script, a rule was added by hand, or a step failed), or the check could not run. The Windows recovery script probes the rules itself and names each failed check by a short token.
alerts.check: the recovery log on Windows (docs/recovery.md): the lines `firewall probe failed: <tokens>` and `firewall still failing after re-apply: <tokens>`; `bin/firewall-check.sh` as root in the container; `iptables -S` there.

parts.policy: the network is not closed by default
parts.web443: web access is not limited to the normal secure port
parts.ssh: secure remote connections are open to servers other than GitHub
parts.lan: part of the private network is open
parts.dns: name lookups are not limited to the trusted lookup server
parts.reject: the final block rule is missing
parts.ollama: the rule for the local model server is missing
parts.ipv6: the newer kind of internet address (IPv6) is not closed
parts.sets: the lists of allowed addresses are missing
parts.unchecked: the protection could not be checked at all
parts.extra: a rule lets traffic through that the firewall setup never creates (for example all outgoing traffic, or plain web on port 80)
parts._other: another problem that this message does not describe yet

alerts.title: a profile has no role, or the role table is broken
alerts.message: The role table has a gap: {problem}. Until it is fixed, that profile can create, complete, claim or delegate nothing, and cannot write to the stack's files or settings.
alerts.action: add the profile's row to the role table (roles.json), or fix the file, then ask your coding agent to re-apply the settings; see STL-CFG-303 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A new Hermes profile was created without a row in docs/hermes-local/roles.json, a row names a profile that no longer exists, or roles.json was edited into invalid JSON or an unknown value.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/roles.py check`; `bin/apply-hermes-local.sh --check` (re-applies with `bin/apply-hermes-local.sh`).

alerts.title: a data file is invalid
alerts.message: A data file that Stella reads is not valid: {problem}. What the file describes is treated as unavailable until it is fixed.
alerts.action: fix the entry the message names, then run the check again. See STL-CFG-310 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A hand edit or a change broke a data file's schema, or an entry names something that does not exist (a provider, a role, a feature).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check` (one line per problem).

alerts.title: a name is not in the data files
alerts.message: A request named something that is not in Stella's data files: {problem}. It was refused and nothing was changed.
alerts.action: add the entry to its data file, or correct the name. See STL-CFG-311 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A typo, or an entry that was never added (a new provider, app, channel, capability or extension).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py list` and `get`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the requested name).

alerts.title: an owner-only action was refused: not the owner's path
alerts.message: An action on an owner-only setting, data file or command was refused because it did not come through the owner's path: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: if this was you, make the change as the owner, through the apply command; if not, look at the card or role the message names. See STL-CFG-312 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A worker or another role tried to read or change an owner-only setting, data file or state file, or to run an owner-only command, or a card branch changed owner data.
alerts.check: the event log and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.
alerts.related: F1 owner-only write path; bin/roles.py, bin/settings.py, bin/stella-apply.py, bin/merge-card.sh

alerts.title: a settings change failed and nothing was changed
alerts.message: A change to a setting or data file failed: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the problem named, then try the change again. See STL-CFG-313 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The new value did not pass the schema or the cross-file rules, or the file could not be written.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`.

alerts.title: a data file or setting was changed by hand
alerts.message: A data file or setting no longer matches what was last applied: {problem}. It was changed outside the apply command.
alerts.action: review the change, then apply it properly or roll it back. See STL-CFG-314 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Someone edited the file directly instead of using the apply command.
alerts.check: the apply command's check mode shows the drift.

alerts.title: a setting value was rejected
alerts.message: A setting value was rejected: {problem}. The old value is still in use.
alerts.action: enter a value in the form the setting allows. See STL-CFG-315 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The value does not match the setting's type or validation in the settings registry.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get settings <key>` shows the allowed form.

alerts.title: there is no backup that can be restored
alerts.message: There is no backup the apply tool can restore or trust: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: do what the message says (it names the backup folder or the file, and the repair). See STL-CFG-316 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The file was never changed through the apply command, its backups were cleaned up, or a backup folder is damaged or was not made by the apply tool.
alerts.check: the backup folder named in `.stella/data-files.json`.

alerts.title: a change needs the owner's confirmation
alerts.message: A change was not made because it needs the owner's confirmation and did not get it: {problem}.
alerts.action: run the change again from a terminal and confirm it when asked. See STL-CFG-317 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The setting is identity-critical, or no terminal was available to ask on.
alerts.check: the setting's sensitivity in `.stella/settings.json`.

alerts.title: the event log could not be written or read
alerts.message: The event log could not be written, or a line of it could not be read: {problem}. A change is never kept without its log line.
alerts.action: fix the log folder (space, permissions), then try the change again; an unreadable line is skipped by readers and can be looked at by hand. See STL-CFG-318 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The disk is full, the folder is read-only, the log file is locked, or a line in the log is not a whole event line.
alerts.check: the event log path in `.stella/data-files.json`; free space and permissions.

alerts.title: a data file is known but not readable through this tool
alerts.message: A request named a data file that Stella knows but is not readable through this tool: {problem}. It was refused and nothing was changed.
alerts.action: the file's keys are read by the apply tool; use that tool, or name a JSON data file. See STL-CFG-319 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The data file is in env format; the owner's file is never opened by this tool.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py list` shows the data files and their formats.

alerts.title: a hard-coded name is used more than its baseline allows
alerts.message: A name that must come from the data files (a provider, model, host, board, project, channel or role) is written into a script or a prompt more often than its baseline allows: {problem}. The lines after this one give each file, the name and the count.
alerts.action: move the value to the data file it belongs in and read it from there, or ask the owner to raise the baseline in hardcode-allow.json. See STL-CFG-320 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A change wrote a name into code or text instead of reading it from data, or removed a use that the baseline still counts.
alerts.check: `bin/hardcode-lint.sh --dump` (every file, name and count); `bin/hardcode-lint.sh` (the uses over the baseline).

alerts.title: a change stopped after it had started
alerts.message: A change to a setting or data file stopped after it had started: {problem}. Now on disk: {detail}.
alerts.action: run the command the message names first; it finishes or undoes the change. See STL-CFG-321 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A write failed (disk full, a folder made read-only, the event log not writable) or the run was interrupted, and putting things back failed too or was not possible after the event line.
alerts.check: `bin/stella-apply.py check <id>`; `bin/stella-apply.py history <id> --json` (the backups and their status).

alerts.title: a check or read of the data files was refused
alerts.message: A check or a read of the data files could not read everything it needed: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the path or the index row the message names, then run the check again. See STL-CFG-322 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A row's file is a link, a hard link, a mount point or not a regular file, two rows name one file, or a name was given in a form the row does not take.
alerts.check: `bin/stella-apply.py check` (one line per problem; the other rows are still checked).

alerts.title: a change of a data file is unfinished
alerts.message: A change to a data file or setting was interrupted and is not finished: {problem}.
alerts.action: run the command the message names; it finishes or undoes the change. See STL-CFG-323 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: An apply or a rollback was stopped (a kill, a crash, a failed write) before its bookkeeping was done.
alerts.check: `bin/stella-apply.py history <id> --json` (the backups and their status).

alerts.title: the same list is kept in two data files
alerts.message: A list of entries is kept in more than one data file: {problem}. The lines after this one name each file, the list kind and the file that owns it or also keeps it.
alerts.action: keep the list only in the file that owns it and refer to its entries by id in the other file; records of their own kind that are keyed by that id are listed under refs in hardcode-allow.json. See STL-CFG-324 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A change copied a list of entries (two or more of the same ids) into a second data file instead of referring to them by id.
alerts.check: `bin/hardcode-lint.sh` (each file and list that is kept twice); the lists rows of docs/hermes-local/hardcode-allow.json (which file owns which list).

alerts.title: a card was not completed: worker identity missing
alerts.message: Card {card} was not completed: the request did not come from that card's own worker run ({missing}). The card stays open.
alerts.action: nothing while its worker is still on it. If the card is stuck, complete it from the command line: see "Completing a stuck card" in SUPERVISOR.md.
alerts.cause: Someone other than the card's worker tried to complete it (the dispatcher, a background review, another card's worker), or the worker's run identity did not reach the guard.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (STL-GRD-601 lines: card, missing, profile); `hermes kanban show <card>` (assignee, runs).

alerts.title: no cards can be created: project list unreadable
alerts.message: No card can be created on board {board} right now: the list of projects bound to it could not be read, so every new card is refused.
alerts.action: ask your coding agent to check the projects list (STL-GRD-602 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: Hermes's projects.db is missing, locked or damaged, or the board has no project bound to it.
alerts.check: `hermes project list`; `hermes project show <slug>` (board, primary folder); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the raw error).

alerts.title: a worker could not be identified
alerts.message: Stella could not tell which card a worker run belongs to ({missing}), so card {card}'s worker cannot write in its own folder. This is a fault in Stella, not in the card or the worker.
alerts.action: nothing on the card. Ask your coding agent to check worker identity (STL-GRD-603 in docs/alert-codes.md); the card's escalation thread opens when its worker stops and asks.
alerts.cause: A builder guard needed the card's worktree and could not prove the run from the board and the process tree while the profile had a running card: the board was unreadable, the run's worker binding was missing, or the hook was not below the bound worker process.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-603`: card, profile and the proof that failed); `hermes kanban show <card> --json` (worker_bound and claimed events of the open run).

alerts.title: a tool call was refused by the rules of its role
alerts.message: A tool call was refused by the rules of the role that made it: {problem}. Nothing was run or changed.
alerts.action: nothing when the role works as designed. If a role needs this tool or command, the owner changes its row in the role table. See STL-GRD-604 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A guard of a role refused a call the role does not allow: a coordinator write, a builder's write outside its card worktree or its git push to main, a reviewer's write, a tool the role names no matcher for, a read of a secret path.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-604`: the role, the card where there is one, and what was refused).
alerts.related: K8, B.1 (F1 W4 round 5); the hooks under docs/hermes-local/hooks/, bin/roles.py hook_refusal

alerts.title: a card's tests could not be run in their box
alerts.message: The tests of a card could not be run in their box: {problem}. The tests never run outside the box, so the step that needed them did not happen.
alerts.action: the merge output says which step stopped: the merge itself (nothing was merged: merge the card again) or, with --push, the push of a main that is already merged locally (the output names the undo). If it happens again, ask your coding agent to check the box (STL-GRD-605 in docs/alert-codes.md).
alerts.cause: The merge runs a card's tests in the OS box, in a throw-away worktree it makes, and with --push the merged main's tests the same way before the push. The box could not start (bubblewrap failed at set-up, no boxed profile without broker variables, a profile folder is missing), the box was ended by a signal, or the throw-away worktree could not be made (a leftover of an earlier run).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-605`: what could not start); `git worktree list` in the repository (a leftover merge-check or merge-test worktree).
alerts.related: K2, F1 W4 round 6; bin/merge-card.sh, bin/box.py merge_exec

alerts.title: a card was not merged: its tests did not pass
alerts.message: A card was not merged because its tests did not pass in their box: {problem}. Nothing was merged.
alerts.action: nothing for the owner unless the card was expected to pass: the lines above this one in the merge output say which test failed. Fix the card, review it and merge again. See STL-GRD-606 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The card's test command ended with a failure in the box. For a card of the stack itself that also covers a test selection that could not be made (the quick list of the test map could not be read) and a suite runner that could not isolate a selftest: both end the run as a failure.
alerts.check: the merge output (the failing test's own lines); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-606`: the branch and how the test command ended).
alerts.related: K2, B2 (F1 W4 round 6, the owner's decision of 2026-11-12 on stack cards); bin/merge-card.sh, bin/selftests.sh, bin/test-map.py

alerts.title: a card was not merged: the main checkout is not ready
alerts.message: A card was not merged because the main checkout is not as a merge needs it: {problem}. Nothing was merged or changed.
alerts.action: the files the message names are the main checkout's own local files, and a merge never replaces or removes them: send the card back so that it no longer carries those paths, or move the files aside yourself, then merge again; never add an ignored file to the repository. For a main checkout that is not clean, put its changes aside first (`git status` lists them). See STL-GRD-607 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The main checkout has changes that are not committed or files git does not track, or the merge would replace or remove a file or folder that exists there and that git does not track (an ignored or untracked local file). A merge never replaces or mixes with such files. Also: the merge made in the main checkout did not produce the tree that was checked beforehand (something in that checkout changes what a merge does there, for example a merge driver or an attribute); it was undone.
alerts.check: `git status` in the main checkout; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-GRD-607`: the paths).
alerts.related: B.3 point 17 (W4-VER3-01), F1 W4 round 6; bin/merge-card.sh

alerts.title: a card was blocked without an escalation
alerts.message: Card {card} ("{title}") was blocked ({by}) and no escalation was opened for it, so it is being posted in #escalations now. Reason: {reason}.
alerts.action: answer in the card's #escalations thread, or archive the card if it is no longer needed.
alerts.cause: Hermes blocked the card without a block event (for example the dispatcher gave up after its retry limit), so the normal escalation hook never ran.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (SILENT_BLOCK for the card); `hermes kanban show <card>` (events).

alerts.title: a worker's model calls keep failing
alerts.message: Card {card}'s worker has had {count} failed model calls in the last {minutes} minutes and has done no work in that time: {parts}. The card stays open while this lasts.
alerts.action: fix what the cause names (start the model server, or load the worker's model and unload others), then wait for the next check; see STL-MDL-701 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The worker's session logged model-call errors (connection errors, stalled streams) and no completed tool call within the window.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (`grep STL-MDL-701`: the model server address and the loaded models); the worker profile's logs/agent.log for the session.
alerts.resolved_title: a worker's model calls work again
alerts.resolved_message: Card {card}'s worker gets model answers again, or the card stopped running. The problem lasted from {since} to {now}.

parts.unreachable: the model server its profile uses does not answer
parts.not_loaded: no model is loaded on that server
parts.other_loaded: another model is loaded on that server instead of the worker's own, likely filling the GPU
parts.loaded: the server answers and the worker's model is loaded, so the calls fail for another reason
parts.unknown: the check could not tell why
parts._other: the check could not tell why

alerts.title: the check for failing model calls cannot run
alerts.message: The check that spots workers whose model calls keep failing could not run {count} times in a row. Until it runs again, a worker stuck on failing model calls is not reported.
alerts.action: see why in .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log ("model watch could not check") and run python3 bin/model_watch.py by hand; usually the board cannot be read or the model_watch settings are invalid (python3 bin/watchdog_settings.py --check); see STL-MDL-702 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: bin/model_watch.py exited non-zero or printed something that is not a JSON list, on several watchdog runs in a row (WATCHDOG_MODEL_WATCH_FAILS_N, default 2).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/watchdog.log; python3 bin/model_watch.py; python3 bin/watchdog_settings.py --check.
alerts.resolved_title: the check for failing model calls runs again
alerts.resolved_message: The check for failing model calls runs again. It could not run from {since} to {now}.

alerts.title: no model link is usable for a request
alerts.message: No model link can serve this request right now: {problem}. The task did not run on any model.
alerts.action: read why each link was left out (the resolver's answer lists every link with its code and reason), then fix the first cause or wait for a cooldown to end. See STL-MDL-710 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Every link of the resolved chain is excluded, needs a grant the owner has not given, or is cooling down after failures.
alerts.check: the resolver's JSON answer (chain[]: status, code, reason); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.title: a model request names something that is not defined
alerts.message: A model request named a role, project, preset, link class, task tier or driver that the data does not define: {problem}. It was refused. Unknown names fail closed.
alerts.action: correct the name, or add the entry to its data file (the role table, role-assignments.json effort_modes, routing.json), then ask again. See STL-MDL-711 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A typo, or an entry that was never added.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the place of the name; its value is never printed).

alerts.title: a CLI login link is refused: terms not recorded
alerts.message: A model link through a logged-in coding CLI was refused because the owner has not recorded that the provider's terms allow this use: {problem}.
alerts.action: if the provider's terms allow it, set terms_ok to true for that connection as the owner (`bin/stella-apply.py apply connections --from <candidate>`, dry run first). See STL-MDL-712 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The connection's type is cli-login and its terms_ok is not true (null, the default, counts as not recorded).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections <id>` (type, terms_ok).
alerts.related: F2 B2, A6; F1b D5; bin/stella_data.py route_problems

alerts.title: an aggregator link is refused: no upstream keys
alerts.message: A model link through an aggregator was refused because its upstream keys do not come from the secrets broker yet: {problem}.
alerts.action: nothing until the secrets broker (phase B1) holds the aggregator's broker entries; the task goes on with its other links. See STL-MDL-713 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The connection is marked aggregator, and its broker_entries cannot be read through the credentials interface (the shipped backend refuses every read).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections <id>` (aggregator, broker_entries); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (credentials).

alerts.title: a hosted link is excluded: secrets or private
alerts.message: A hosted model link was excluded because the card carries secrets or vault content, or its project is marked private: {problem}. No grant, setting or preset changes this.
alerts.action: nothing if that is intended: such work stays on local links. If the card's facts are missing or wrong, record them on the host (the card facts store). See STL-MDL-714 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The card facts say carries_secrets or vault_content (a missing record or field always counts as holding), or the data policy marks the project private.
alerts.check: the card's record in the card facts store (index key card_facts); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get data-policy` (projects, private).
alerts.related: F2 B6, A8, design-check DC-01, DC-03; .stella/routing.json card_facts

alerts.title: a model does not meet the role's requirements
alerts.message: A model link was left out because its model does not meet what the role requires: {problem}.
alerts.action: use a link whose probe record meets them, or probe the link again if the model changed (`probe.py run --again`). See STL-MDL-715 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The role's requirements (tool calling, vision, smallest context size) against the link's capability probe record (F2b): a record that fails one (or a null capability) excludes the link, and the context size is the probed effective context; with resolve --tokens N, a link whose probed effective context is below N is left out too. A link with no record is not left out (it serves unproven, STL-MDL-738).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/roles.py requirements <role>`; `python3 bin/probe.py show --connection <id> --model <model> --json`.
alerts.related: F2 B2, F2b B2 and item C; bin/stella_data.py probed, unmet

alerts.title: the data policy forbids a model link
alerts.message: A model link was left out because the data policy does not allow it for this project or for the data the role handles: {problem}.
alerts.action: nothing if that is intended. To allow it, the owner changes the data policy (the project's mode, its allowed providers, a class rule) or the connection (data_classes_allowed, allowed_roles, enabled). See STL-MDL-716 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The project's mode (Local only, allowed providers), a connection that is switched off or does not list the role or its data classes, or a data class that never reaches a hosted link.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get data-policy`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections <id>`.
alerts.related: F2 B4, B6; bin/stella_data.py policy_allows, route_problems

alerts.title: a model link needs a privacy grant
alerts.message: A model link can be used only after the owner accepts a privacy grant: {problem}. It was not skipped and it was not used.
alerts.action: accept or refuse the request in the approval popup; an acceptance holds for one project or Stella-wide until you revoke it. See STL-MDL-717 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The role handles a data class whose hosted rule is grant, the link leaves the machine, and no privacy grant in force names this connection for this project.
alerts.check: the approval request (`python3 bin/approvals.py status <id>`); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get data-policy` (privacy_grants: scope, revoked_at).
alerts.related: F2 B6, A8; bin/stella_data.py grant_in_force, route_problems

alerts.title: a last-resort link needs the owner's acceptance
alerts.message: The only links left are of the active preset's last-resort class, which is used only after the owner accepts the crossing: {problem}.
alerts.action: accept or refuse the request in the approval popup; an acceptance holds for one project or Stella-wide until you revoke it. See STL-MDL-718 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Every link of the preset's class order is excluded, failing or cooling down, and no crossing grant in force covers this preset and class for this project.
alerts.check: the approval request (`python3 bin/approvals.py status <id>`); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get grants` (crossing_grants: scope, revoked_at).
alerts.related: F2 B3, A3, A4; bin/stella_data.py grant_in_force; .stella/grants.json crossing_grants

alerts.title: a task waits for the owner's acceptance
alerts.message: A task is paused until the owner answers a routing consent request: {problem}.
alerts.action: answer the approval popup (accept or refuse). See STL-MDL-719 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The task's next model link needs a grant the owner has not given, and unattended run mode is off (or the task has no card, so no request can be raised for it).
alerts.check: the approval request (`python3 bin/approvals.py status <id>`); .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.title: a task is queued until the owner grants a link
alerts.message: A task was queued because its next model link needs a grant the owner has not given, and unattended run mode is on: {problem}.
alerts.action: give the grant as the owner (for one project or Stella-wide), or leave the task queued. See STL-MDL-720 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Unattended run mode is on, so no popup waits: the task is queued and this alert is its one notice.
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (consent).

alerts.title: a task moved to the next model link
alerts.message: A task moved to another model link after a failure: {problem}.
alerts.action: nothing; the failed link cools down and is used again once it recovers. See STL-MDL-721 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A rate limit or daily cap, a timeout or server error, a malformed tool call, a model that no longer exists, or a context window too small for the task.
alerts.check: the event log (one line per switch); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (failover).

alerts.title: a mid-task switch to a model link was refused
alerts.message: A switch to another model link in the middle of a task was refused: {problem}. The link after it was tried instead.
alerts.action: nothing; to let this link take over mid-task, give the task a model with a larger context window. See STL-MDL-722 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The new model's probed effective context (its probe record; no record counts as too small) does not hold the conversation so far, or the tool call in progress cannot carry over to it.
alerts.check: the event log (the switch line); `python3 bin/probe.py show --json` (context.effective).
alerts.related: F2 B5, A7; F2b item C (probe data)

alerts.title: failover stopped: the task ran out of links
alerts.message: Failover stopped for a task: {problem}. It never goes back to a link the task already used, and it stops after the allowed number of switches.
alerts.action: look at why the links failed (the task's failure history), then run the task again once one of them works. See STL-MDL-723 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Every remaining link was already visited in this task, or the task reached routing.json failover.max_switches_per_task.
alerts.check: the event log (the task's switch lines); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (failover.max_switches_per_task).

alerts.title: a model link is cooling down
alerts.message: A model link is not used for now because it failed recently: {problem}. It is tried again when the cooldown ends.
alerts.action: nothing; one success after the cooldown clears it. See STL-MDL-724 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A failure put the link (or every link of its connection) in cooldown; the time doubles with each repeated failure up to the trigger's cap.
alerts.check: the resolver's JSON answer (chain[].cooldown_until); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (failover.triggers).
alerts.related: F2 B5, A7; features stub routing-observed-quota

alerts.title: a preset turns off a role the workflow requires
alerts.message: A routing preset turns off a role that the workflow requires: {problem}. The data is treated as not valid until it is fixed.
alerts.action: set the role active again in that preset (role-assignments.json effort_modes, roles), or give it a class order, then run the check again. See STL-MDL-725 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The preset sets active false for a role that routing.json workflow.required_roles lists as always, or under a trigger that can fire; or it leaves such a role active with no link that can serve it (the connection, model and role rules; or, resting on probe data, every such link has a probe record that fails the role's requirements: that line writes one alert and never stops a read).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (workflow).
alerts.related: F2 B3, A9, A10, design D1.9; .stella/routing.json workflow

alerts.title: a preset link fails the role's requirements
alerts.message: A pin or a fallback that a routing preset gives an active role does not meet the role's requirements: {problem}. The data is treated as not valid until it is fixed.
alerts.action: name a model that is listed for its connection and that the preset, connection and role rules allow, then run the check again. See STL-MDL-726 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The model is not listed for its connection; or the link's connection is switched off, does not list the role, does not allow every data class the role handles, or lies outside the localities the preset allows; or the preset leaves an active role with no link that these rules allow. Or the link's capability probe record fails the role's requirements (tool calling, vision, effective context), or every link these rules allow has such a record: a line that rests on probe data writes one alert and never stops a read (a link with no record is not refused here).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`; `python3 bin/roles.py requirements <role>`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections <id>`; `python3 bin/probe.py show --json`.
alerts.related: F2 B3, A9, design D1.9; bin/stella_data.py link_problems

alerts.title: a built-in preset cannot be changed
alerts.message: A change to the routing presets was refused because it changes, removes or adds a built-in preset: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: leave the built-in presets as they are; to route your own way, copy one under a new id (based_on names the original) and select that. See STL-MDL-727 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The candidate differs from the file in a preset marked builtin true, drops it, or marks another preset builtin true. Only the weekly model check (F2c) and a signed release (E1) update those.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella-apply.py apply role-assignments --from <candidate> --dry-run`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get role-assignments` (effort_modes, builtin).
alerts.related: F2 B3, design D1.9; features stub builtin-preset-updater

alerts.title: a key could not be read from the key store
alerts.message: A model key was not read: {problem}. The call was not made, and no key was printed or logged.
alerts.action: nothing until the secrets broker (phase B1) is the backend; a link that needs a key is left out until then. See STL-MDL-728 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The credentials backend in use refuses every read (the shipped one), the name is not in it, or the read was asked from a worker environment.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (credentials.backend, backends).
alerts.related: F2 B8, design D3, design-check DC-05; .stella/routing.json credentials

alerts.title: a task moved to a less private kind of model
alerts.message: A task now uses a model link of a less private class than the one its chain starts with: {problem}. It is allowed (a grant covers it where one is needed); this is your notice.
alerts.action: nothing if that is fine. To stop it, revoke the grant, or select a preset or a project mode that keeps the work on more private links. See STL-MDL-729 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A pick or a failover switch went to a link class whose privacy_rank is higher than that of the first class of the resolved chain.
alerts.check: the event log (the switch line); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get routing` (link_classes: privacy_rank).
alerts.related: F2 B6, B7, A8, design-check DC-07; .stella/routing.json consent.alert_code_notice

alerts.title: the escalation walk is not built yet
alerts.message: A request for the next rung of a role's escalation chain was refused: {problem}. The chain is stored, and nothing climbs it until phase F2b.
alerts.action: nothing until F2b builds the walk. See STL-MDL-730 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Phase F2 stored each role's escalation chain and built no walk. Retired in F2b: the walk is `resolve --rung` (STL-MDL-731, STL-MDL-732).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py stubs --phase F2b`.
alerts.related: F2 B3, design D1.8; F2b item D

alerts.title: no higher rung: escalate to the owner
alerts.message: The escalation chain has no usable rung for this request: {problem}. Nothing climbs further; the work goes to you.
alerts.action: read the answer's rung.skipped (each skipped rung with its code and reason): grant the crossing, fix the first cause, or add a rung to the role's escalation_chain in a custom preset; else decide on the card yourself. See STL-MDL-731 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: resolve --rung N asked past the last rung, the role has no escalation_chain under the active preset, or every rung from N on is excluded or waits for a grant.
alerts.check: the resolver's JSON answer (rung: requested, last, skipped[]); the event log (routing.rung-skipped, routing.rung-exhausted lines).
alerts.related: F2b item D (design-D.md); .stella/role-assignments.json effort_modes roles escalation_chain

alerts.title: a rung of the escalation chain was skipped
alerts.message: A rung of the escalation chain was skipped because the preset's boundary or the data policy forbids it, or it waits for a grant: {problem}. The walk went on to the next rung.
alerts.action: nothing if that is intended. To allow the rung, give the grant it waits for, or change the policy that excludes it. See STL-MDL-732 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The rung's link fails a rule of the chain (hard exclusion, data policy, Local only, the connection, the role's requirements, the preset's classes and localities) or needs a crossing or privacy grant that is not in force.
alerts.check: the event log (routing.rung-skipped lines: role, preset, rung, link, status, code); the resolver's JSON answer (rung.skipped[]).

alerts.title: the probe was asked about a link the catalog lacks
alerts.message: The capability probe refused a link that is not in the connections catalog, or whose model the connection's model list does not show: {problem}. Nothing was probed or recorded.
alerts.action: check the connection and model ids (`python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections`), or add the model to the catalog first. See STL-MDL-734 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: probe.py run named a connection or a model that is not there (or not listed by the connection), and a probe is never made for a link the catalog does not hold.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections`; `python3 bin/probe.py due --json`.

alerts.title: this model version was already probed
alerts.message: The capability probe refused to probe a model version it already holds a record for: {problem}. Nothing was called and nothing was changed.
alerts.action: nothing if the record is current. To probe the same version again, run probe.py run with --again. See STL-MDL-735 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A record for this connection, model and version exists, and a probe runs once per model version.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/probe.py show --json`.

alerts.title: a link gave no answer a probe or call could use
alerts.message: A link could not be probed, or a structured-output call got no valid answer from it after its repair retry: {problem}. Nothing was recorded, and no guessed value was used.
alerts.action: check that the connection is reachable and its key is in place, then run the probe again; for a structured call, the link may not follow the schema (try another link). See STL-MDL-736 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The model list or the probe's calls got no answer, or an answer that is not JSON that meets the schema, even after the one repair retry.
alerts.check: the command's output; `python3 bin/probe.py show --json`.

alerts.title: the triage router could not give a verdict
alerts.message: The triage router could not classify an input: {problem}. No verdict was made and nothing was routed.
alerts.action: check that the router role has a local link that answers (`python3 bin/resolve.py resolve --role <router role> --project '' --json`) and that the routing data's triage block is consistent, then try again. See STL-MDL-740 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The router role's link was refused or gave no readable answer (a non-JSON answer is not this: that is an unsure verdict), or the routing triage block is wrong.
alerts.check: the command's output; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get --json routing` (triage).
alerts.related: F2b item F; bin/triage.py (the routing data triage block)

alerts.title: a triage label was refused
alerts.message: A triage label was refused: {problem}. Nothing was recorded.
alerts.action: give the id of a verdict that `triage.py route` printed, a route of the routing data's triage tiers (or its image route) and the source override or reroute. See STL-MDL-741 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The id is no logged triage verdict, or the route is outside the tiers.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/event_log.py tail --json -n 50` (type triage.verdict).
alerts.related: F2b item F; bin/triage.py (the routing data triage block)

alerts.title: the triage threshold could not be fitted or read
alerts.message: The triage calibration was refused: {problem}. The threshold was not changed.
alerts.action: label more verdicts (`triage.py label`) until the routing data's triage min_labels is reached, or remove or repair the calibration file named by the data index key triage_calibration. See STL-MDL-742 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Fewer labelled verdicts than triage.min_labels, or the calibration file cannot be read or is invalid.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/triage.py fit --json`; the file the index key triage_calibration names.
alerts.related: F2b item F; bin/triage.py (the routing data triage block)

alerts.title: the build team preset cannot be generated
alerts.message: The build team could not be generated or checked: {problem}. Nothing was written.
alerts.action: name a preset that has agents (`--preset`, or the data index key team_preset), and give every agent a body file in the folder of the index key team_bodies, then run it again. See STL-MDL-743 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The preset is not in the role-assignments data or has no agents, or an agent has no body text file.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get --json role-assignments`; the folder of the index key team_bodies.

alerts.title: an agent file differs from the build team preset
alerts.message: The build team check found a file that differs from its preset: {problem}.
alerts.action: generate the files again (`python3 bin/team.py generate --json`) and commit them; change an agent in the preset and its body file, never in the generated file. See STL-MDL-744 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: An agent file was edited by hand, is missing, or belongs to an agent the preset no longer has.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/team.py check --json` (agents[].problems, stale).

alerts.title: an agent ran on a model its preset does not list
alerts.message: The build team check found a session whose agent ran on a model its preset does not list: {problem}.
alerts.action: find out why the agent ran on that model (a changed agent file not yet loaded, or a hand-set model), then fix the preset or the file. See STL-MDL-745 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: In the latest session log an agent's transcript shows a model that is not its link, a fallback or a rung.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/team.py check --json` (agents[].session).

alerts.title: cross-family review was waived for a reviewer
alerts.message: A review role was answered without a link of another model family than the card's builder (cross-family review waived): {problem}.
alerts.action: nothing if that is intended. For cross-family review, set cross_family_review true on the preset, probe the links (`python3 bin/probe.py due`), or make a link of another family reachable in the reviewer's class order. See STL-MDL-737 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The preset does not ask for cross-family review, the builder's family is not known (no probe record), or no usable link of the reviewer has another family where the chain may be reordered (inside one class-order item, never past a more private link).
alerts.check: the event log (routing.cross-family-waiver lines: card, role, preset, families, reason); the resolver's JSON answer (cross_family).
alerts.related: F2b B2, A4 and item C (design-C.md); bin/resolve.py crossed, bin/route.py

alerts.title: a link with no probe record serves a role
alerts.message: A model link that has no capability probe record was picked or listed for a role with requirements, or for a task whose size is given: {problem}. It may serve, but what it can do is not proven.
alerts.action: run `python3 bin/probe.py due` and probe the links it lists (`probe.py run`); a CLI-login link cannot be probed and stays flagged. See STL-MDL-738 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The link was never probed (a fresh install, a new model) or cannot be probed (a CLI login). Owner ruling 2026-11-18: such a link may serve a role with requirements, or a task whose size is given (resolve --tokens, route.py's prompt size), flagged once per pick; `check` lists it as a warning, never as a problem. A pick whose flag line cannot be written is not served (STL-CFG-318).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/probe.py due --json` (due, unprobeable); `python3 bin/probe.py show --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check` (warning lines).
alerts.related: F2b item C (design-C.md, owner ruling 2026-11-18); bin/stella_data.py needs_probe, bin/route.py, bin/resolve.py

alerts.title: the probe records file cannot be used
alerts.message: The capability probe records file is present but cannot be used: {problem}. Until it is fixed no model link counts as probed, so a role with requirements gets no link.
alerts.action: run `python3 bin/probe.py check --json` to see the problem; `python3 bin/probe.py run --connection <id> --model <model> --again` drops a bad record and writes a good one; a file that cannot be read at all is fixed or moved aside by the owner. See STL-MDL-739 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A record that fails the records schema, a record key twice, an output shape the routing data no longer lists (routing probe.output_shapes edited), or a file that cannot be read (too big, a symbolic link, not JSON). A missing file is no problem (no record: a fresh install). Routing fails closed on it (F2b CRT-01): no link looks unprobed.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/probe.py check --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`; the probe_records path in `.stella/data-files.json`.
alerts.related: F2b item C (CRT-01); bin/stella_data.py probe_records, bin/probe.py read and save

alerts.title: an escalation rung is not on this script's CLI
alerts.message: An escalation call was refused because the rung the resolver served runs on a connection that is not the coding tool the escalation script drives: {problem}. Nothing was run or queued, and no other rung was tried.
alerts.action: make that rung of the role's escalation_chain a link of the connection whose `cli` is the script's CLI, in a custom preset, or decide on the card yourself. See STL-MDL-746 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The role's escalation chain (the active preset) holds, at the card's current rung, a link of another connection: escalate.sh runs one CLI only and never climbs past a served rung by itself.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (event NOT_THIS_CLI); `bin/resolve.py resolve --role <role> --project <project> --card <card> --rung <rung> --json` (rung.link.connection).

alerts.title: an escalation call names no known purpose or rung
alerts.message: An escalation call was refused before any model was asked: {problem}. Nothing was run or queued.
alerts.action: call the escalation script with a card, a purpose of routing.json escalation.purposes and a reason (the caller names no model), or fix state/rungs.json (per card and role, a whole number from 1). See STL-MDL-747 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The purpose has no row in the routing data's escalation.purposes (a caller still naming a model gets its model read as the purpose), or the host-side rung state of the card cannot be read or holds no whole number from 1.
alerts.check: .supervisor/escalations.log (event USAGE or RUNG_STATE); `python3 bin/stella_data.py get --json routing` (escalation.purposes).
alerts.related: F2b item E (design-E.md, owner decision 2026-11-18: the purpose picks the role); bin/escalate.sh

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: provider not allowed
alerts.message: An owner proof was refused because its provider is not in the policy, is switched off, or is not one this action allows: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make the change again with a proof the owner-auth policy allows for it (.stella/owner-auth.json, actions); an account login is never an owner proof. See STL-OWN-801 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A proof named a provider that is not in the owner-auth policy, is disabled, or is in no alternative of the action class asked for.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: not valid
alerts.message: An owner proof was refused because it is not valid (wrong signature, edited fields, wrong user or message): {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make a new proof on the host (owner_auth.py prove) or answer again from the owner's own account on the delivered message; if this was not you, someone tried to forge an owner proof. See STL-OWN-802 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A proof whose signature or MAC does not match its fields, a malformed proof, or a channel answer from another user id or on another message than the one delivered.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: expired
alerts.message: An owner proof was refused because it has expired: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make a new proof and use it within its lifetime (owner-auth policy proof_ttl_s). See STL-OWN-803 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The proof's expires_at is in the past.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: already used
alerts.message: An owner proof was refused because it was already used once (a replay): {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make a new proof for this change; if you did not use it twice, someone replayed it. See STL-OWN-804 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The proof's nonce is already recorded in the approval store (approval_store/nonces): every proof counts once.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: for another action
alerts.message: An owner proof was refused because it was made for another action than this one: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make a proof for exactly this change (target, old and new value). See STL-OWN-805 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The proof's digest is not the digest of the action asked for (another target, old or new value).
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: the owner key is missing or unsafe
alerts.message: The owner key cannot be used: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: on the host, as the owner: create the key with owner_auth.py init-key if there is none; if it exists, make it a plain file of your own user with mode 0600 and one link, or, if you did not change it, treat it as compromised: remove it and create a new one. See STL-OWN-806 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: No owner key file at the index owner_key yet, or the file is a symbolic link, has another owner, a mode other than 0600, a second hard link, or does not hold a key.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: the owner key already exists
alerts.message: The owner key was not created because one already exists: {problem}. The existing key was not changed.
alerts.action: nothing to do if the key is yours; to replace it, remove the old key on the host first, knowing that proofs made with it stop working. See STL-OWN-807 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: owner_auth.py init-key never overwrites an existing owner key.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: the confirmation phrase is missing or wrong
alerts.message: An identity-critical change was refused because its confirmation phrase is missing or wrong: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make the change again on the host terminal and type the phrase exactly as shown, or sign it on a paired device with the phrase. See STL-OWN-808 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The typed-phrase provider found no terminal or read another text than the phrase; or the device-phrase provider found no device-signed phrase equal to it.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: an owner-auth provider command failed
alerts.message: An owner proof was refused because the provider's command failed or took too long: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: check the provider's command (owner-auth policy, its argv and timeout_s) and try again. See STL-OWN-809 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A command provider exited non-zero, could not start, or ran past its timeout_s.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; owner_auth.py check.

alerts.title: a stub is due and still listed
alerts.message: A stub is due at or before this phase and is still listed: {problem}.
alerts.action: build what replaces it (features.json replaced_by), then remove the stub entry, or, if the plan moved, change its due_phase as the owner. See STL-OWN-810 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: stella_data.py stubs --phase found a features entry whose due_phase is at or before that phase.
alerts.check: stella_data.py stubs --phase <phase>; .stella/features.json (due_phase, replaced_by, phase_order).

alerts.title: an approval answer names no request of the service
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because it names no request the approval service made: {problem}. Nothing was decided.
alerts.action: none, unless you expected that request: then look for it with `bin/approvals.py status <id>`. See STL-OWN-820 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The answer's request id is not in the approval store, or the store record has no trusted approval-request line (it was not made by bin/approvals.py).
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval answer came after the decision
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because its request was already decided (a replay): {problem}. The first decision stands.
alerts.action: none; a decision is final. Ask for a new approval if it must change. See STL-OWN-821 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The same answer was collected twice, or a second answer (approve or deny) came for a decided request.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval answer came after expiry
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because its request expired: {problem}. Nothing was approved.
alerts.action: ask for a new approval if the action is still wanted. See STL-OWN-822 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The answer arrived after the request's expires_at.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval answer has the wrong nonce
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because it does not carry its request's nonce: {problem}. Nothing was decided.
alerts.action: none, unless the answer was yours: then answer the request's own message again. See STL-OWN-823 in docs/alert-codes.md.
