alerts.cause: The answer was made for another request, or its nonce was changed.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval answer is for another action
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because the action digest it carries is not the request's: {problem}. Nothing was decided.
alerts.action: look at what was shown and answer the request again if the action is the one you meant. See STL-OWN-824 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The action changed after it was shown, or the answer was made for another action.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval answer is not on its request's message
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because it is not on the message the request was delivered as on that channel: {problem}. Nothing was decided.
alerts.action: answer on the request's own message (or thread). See STL-OWN-825 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The answer was given on another message, or the request was never delivered on that channel.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: a channel of this kind may not answer approvals
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because its channel's kind may not answer approvals: {problem}. Text from cards, comments, tool or model output is never an answer.
alerts.action: none; answer on a channel the owner-auth policy lets answer (.stella/owner-auth.json, channel_kinds). See STL-OWN-826 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The channel's kind is false in the policy's channel_kinds, or not listed there (an unknown kind answers nothing).
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: a voice answer outside the host-confirmation entry
alerts.message: A voice answer was refused: a voice channel answers no approval, except the quick confirmation of the voice profile's own ask-first host action when the policy's voice_host_confirmation entry is on: {problem}. Nothing was decided.
alerts.action: answer on another channel; or, for the voice profile's own host action, check the entry (.stella/owner-auth.json, voice_host_confirmation). See STL-OWN-827 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The entry is off, or the request is of another class or requester, its ttl is longer than max_ttl_s, or the answer did not carry the digest of the details shown (a changed target).
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval answer is not proven to be the owner's
alerts.message: An approval answer was refused because the owner proof for it failed: {problem}. Nothing was decided.
alerts.action: answer yourself, from the owner's account on that channel (or with the owner key on the host). See STL-OWN-828 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The answer came from another user id, or owner_auth.require refused the proof (its own code is named in the problem).
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval request is not well formed
alerts.message: An approval request or ask was refused because it is not well formed: {problem}. No request was made.
alerts.action: fix the asking command (class, action, summary, card, ttl); an agent asks with `bin/event_untrusted.py append --type approval-ask`. See STL-OWN-829 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The class is not an approval class of the request schema, the action is not an action object, a text is missing, or the ttl is not a whole number of seconds.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: an approval channel adapter failed
alerts.message: A channel adapter of the approval service failed: {problem}. Nothing was decided by it.
alerts.action: check the channel's adapter (.stella/channels.json, its deliver or collect argv) and the channel itself, then run the command again. See STL-OWN-830 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The adapter could not start, exited non-zero, ran past adapter_timeout_s, gave no message ref, or printed a line that is not an answer.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.title: the resume after an approval decision failed
alerts.message: The decision on an approval was recorded, but resuming its card failed: {problem}.
alerts.action: resume the card by hand (unblock it with the decision as the reason). See STL-OWN-831 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The resume command (.stella/channels.json, resume) could not start, exited non-zero or ran past its timeout_s.
alerts.check: the command output and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/approvals.py status <id> --json`.

alerts.related: F1c B7 trusted event log; bin/event_log.py
alerts.title: an event log line was edited or forged
alerts.message: A line of the trusted event log does not match its seal: {problem}. It counts for nothing, and the log can no longer be trusted as a whole.
alerts.action: do not trust the log's lines from that point as proof; find which process wrote the file. See STL-EVT-901 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Someone or something changed the line after it was written, or wrote a line without the writer key (a made-up seal).
alerts.check: `bin/event_log.py verify` (it names every problem with its line); the event log path and event_writer_state in `.stella/data-files.json`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.related: F1c B7 trusted event log; bin/event_log.py
alerts.title: an event log line was deleted
alerts.message: A line of the trusted event log is missing: {problem}. The log can no longer be trusted as a whole.
alerts.action: do not trust the log's lines from that point as proof; find which process wrote the file. See STL-EVT-902 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A line was removed from the middle or the end of the log (its sequence number is skipped, or the log ends before the writer's last line).
alerts.check: `bin/event_log.py verify` (it names every problem with its line); the event log path and event_writer_state in `.stella/data-files.json`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.related: F1c B7 trusted event log; bin/event_log.py
alerts.title: event log lines were reordered or replayed
alerts.message: The trusted event log is out of order: {problem}. A copied or moved line counts once, in its first place.
alerts.action: do not trust the log's lines from that point as proof; find which process wrote the file. See STL-EVT-903 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Lines were swapped, or a genuine line was copied to another place in the log.
alerts.check: `bin/event_log.py verify` (it names every problem with its line); the event log path and event_writer_state in `.stella/data-files.json`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.related: F1c B7 trusted event log; bin/event_log.py
alerts.title: a line was inserted into the event log
alerts.message: A line without the writer's seal sits in the trusted event log after its chain started: {problem}. It counts for nothing.
alerts.action: do not trust the log's lines from that point as proof; find which process wrote the file. See STL-EVT-904 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A line was written into the trusted log by something other than the writer (agents must use the untrusted stream, bin/event_untrusted.py).
alerts.check: `bin/event_log.py verify` (it names every problem with its line); the event log path and event_writer_state in `.stella/data-files.json`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.related: F1c B7 trusted event log; bin/event_log.py
alerts.title: the event writer state is missing or unsafe
alerts.message: The event writer's state (its key and last line) is missing, unreadable or unsafe: {problem}. Nothing was written, and no line can be checked.
alerts.action: restore the writer state from a backup if you have one; never delete the log to start again. See STL-EVT-905 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The state file was deleted, its mode is not 0600, it is a link or has a second link, it belongs to another user, or its content is broken.
alerts.check: `bin/event_log.py verify` (it names every problem with its line); the event log path and event_writer_state in `.stella/data-files.json`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.related: F1c B7 trusted event log; bin/event_log.py
alerts.title: an event log line names another writer
alerts.message: A line of the trusted event log names a writer that is not this one, or a writer install that is not the line's own: {problem}. It counts for nothing.
alerts.action: do not trust the log's lines from that point as proof; find which process wrote the file. See STL-EVT-906 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The line was forged with another writer id, or its writer install id was changed. (An install id changed since the line was written is no forgery; a line copied from another install fails its mac: STL-EVT-901.)
alerts.check: `bin/event_log.py verify` (it names every problem with its line); the event log path and event_writer_state in `.stella/data-files.json`; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: device not paired
alerts.message: A device-signed owner proof was refused because its device is not paired: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: pair the device first (an owner write of the devices row on the host); if you do not know this device, someone is trying to act as you. See STL-OWN-811 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The proof's device_id is not an entry of the device registry (index row devices).
alerts.check: the command output; bin/devices.py list --json; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.title: an owner proof was refused: device revoked
alerts.message: A device-signed owner proof was refused because its device is revoked: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: use a paired device; if this device was revoked because it was lost, someone may hold it. See STL-OWN-812 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The device's registry entry has revoked_at set.
alerts.check: the command output; bin/devices.py list --json; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.title: remote owner changes: rate limit reached
alerts.message: An owner change from a remote device was refused because the rate limit for remote owner changes is reached: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: wait for the window to pass, or make the change on the host; if you did not make the earlier changes, revoke the device. See STL-OWN-813 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: More device-signed owner changes were accepted within the window than the owner-auth policy remote.rate_limit allows.
alerts.check: the command output; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the remote change alerts); owner-auth policy remote.

alerts.title: the primary lease is held by another engine
alerts.message: The primary lease was refused: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: only one engine per account is the primary; move the primary with a planned hand-over, or wait until the lease expires. See STL-OWN-814 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Another engine holds the account's primary lease and it has not expired (or the engine releasing it is not its holder).
alerts.check: the command output; lease_double.py show --state <file> --account <account> (test double; U1 builds the real lease).

alerts.title: an owner change was made from a remote device
alerts.message: An owner change was accepted from a paired remote device: {problem}.
alerts.action: nothing if it was you; if not, revoke that device at once (owner write of the devices row on the host) and check what changed. See STL-OWN-815 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A device-signature proof passed for an owner action; every remote owner change raises this alert (owner-auth policy remote.alert_code).
alerts.check: the event log line of the change; bin/devices.py list --json; .supervisor/logs/alerts.log.

alerts.title: something needs a look
alerts.message: A part of Stella reported a problem, but its description is missing from the alert list ({requested}). {summary}
alerts.action: see STL-GEN-000 in docs/alert-codes.md, and ask your coding agent to add the missing description.
alerts.cause: A script asked for an alert code that is not in docs/hermes-local/alert-catalog.json, or the alert could not be rendered (catalog unreadable, python3 missing).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (the requested code and the raw details).

alerts.title: a loopback API request was refused: wrong Host
alerts.message: A request to the local API was refused because its Host header is not this API's own address: {problem}. Nothing was done.
alerts.action: none if you did not send it: a web page tried to reach the API under another name (DNS rebinding). If you did, send it to an allowed loopback host with the API's port. See STL-OWN-850 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The Host header is missing, has no port or another port, or names a host that is not in the contract's hosts list.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: a loopback API request was refused: foreign Origin
alerts.message: A request to the local API was refused because it came from a web page the API does not allow: {problem}. Nothing was done.
alerts.action: none if you did not send it: a web page in your browser tried to use the API. If a page of yours needs it, add its origin to the contract's origins (an owner change). See STL-OWN-851 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The request carries an Origin header (null included) that is not in the contract's origins list; this holds for every method and scope.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: a loopback API request was refused: no Origin
alerts.message: A request that changes something was refused because it does not say which page sent it: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: send state-changing requests from an allowed page (they carry an Origin), or add the Origin header your client should send. See STL-OWN-852 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A request with a method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS carries no Origin header.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: a loopback API request was refused: CSRF token
alerts.message: A request that changes something was refused because its CSRF token is missing or wrong: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: none if you did not send it (a cross-site request). If you did, reload the page to get the current CSRF token and send it again. See STL-OWN-853 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A request with a method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS has no CSRF header, or its value is not the session's CSRF token.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: a loopback API request was refused: API token
alerts.message: A request to the local API was refused because its API token is missing or wrong: {problem}. Nothing was done.
alerts.action: send the current API token in the contract's token header; if you did not send this request, nothing is needed. See STL-OWN-854 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The request has no token header, or its value is not the session's API token. Every endpoint, read scope included, needs it.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: an owner write was refused: no owner proof
alerts.message: An owner write through the local API was refused because it carries no owner proof: {problem}. The API token alone is never enough. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make an owner proof for this request on the host (owner_auth.py prove --class with the contract's owner_class) and send it in the proof header. See STL-OWN-855 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The endpoint's scope is owner-write and the request has no proof header.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: an owner write was refused: owner proof refused
alerts.message: An owner write through the local API was refused because its owner proof does not hold: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: look up the cause code in this table (STL-OWN-80x), make a new proof for exactly this method, path and body, and send it again. See STL-OWN-856 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The proof header is not JSON, or owner_auth.require refused the proof (the cause: another action or body 805, already used 804, expired 803, invalid 802, provider not allowed 801).
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: loopback API request refused: endpoint not listed
alerts.message: A request to the local API was refused because no endpoint of the contract has that method and path: {problem}. Nothing was done.
alerts.action: check the method and the exact path (a trailing slash or a query string is another path); a new endpoint is a new row of the contract (an owner change). See STL-OWN-857 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The method and exact path are not a row of the contract's endpoints.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: the loopback API guard cannot judge requests
alerts.message: The local API refused a request because its guard cannot judge it: {problem}. Everything is refused until this is fixed.
alerts.action: run `bin/stella_data.py check loopback-api` and fix the contract, or restart the API with a valid session. See STL-OWN-858 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The loopback-api contract is missing, unreadable or invalid (its schema, three distinct header names, each method and path once), the session lacks its API token, CSRF token or bound port, or the request could not be read.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: the loopback API double cannot start
alerts.message: The loopback API test double did not start: {problem}.
alerts.action: run it again with --port 0 (a free port), or free the port it was given. See STL-OWN-859 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The loopback port it was given cannot be bound.
alerts.check: the HTTP answer's code and message, and .supervisor/logs/alerts.log; `bin/loopback_guard.py check <request.json>` replays a request.

alerts.title: a remote owner change was refused: no alert
alerts.message: A remote owner change was refused because its alert could not be written: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make the alert log writable again (.supervisor/logs/alerts.log is a file the stack can append to), then send the request again from the device; its proof was not spent. See STL-OWN-816 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Every owner change from a remote device raises an alert (B6), and the alert line is written before the change counts; the alert log could not be written (a folder in its place, a full disk, no permission).
alerts.check: .supervisor/logs/alerts.log (type, owner, mode); free disk space; ESCALATE_SUP_DIR when set.
alerts.related: F1c B6, D5; bin/owner_auth.py remote_change, .stella/owner-auth.json remote

alerts.title: a comparison was given records it cannot use
alerts.message: bin/compare.py refused its input: {problem}. Nothing was compared and nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the records file (a JSON list of objects with task, trial, passed and an optional score) and run the command again. See STL-MDL-750 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: compare.py compare or stats was given a file it cannot read, that is not a JSON list, or whose records lack a task, a boolean passed or a score from 0 to 1.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/compare.py compare --a A.json --b B.json --json`.

alerts.title: a candidate broke a task of the regression set
alerts.message: The candidate fails a task that earlier failed cards fixed and that must keep passing: {problem}. The comparison is refused whatever the mean score; nothing was changed.
alerts.action: do not switch to this candidate; look at the named tasks. See STL-MDL-751 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: compare.py compare was given a regression set and the candidate's trials of a set task passed less often than model-check.json regression_set.min_pass_rate, or were missing.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/compare.py compare --a A.json --b B.json --regression R.json --json` names the tasks in `failed`.

alerts.title: the comparison parameters cannot be used
alerts.message: bin/compare.py cannot use .stella/model-check.json: {problem}. No comparison was made and no routing statistic was computed.
alerts.action: fix the file (`python3 bin/stella_data.py check` names the problem), then run `python3 bin/compare.py check`. See STL-MDL-752 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The comparison parameters file is missing, fails its schema, or asks for pass_k above trials.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`; `python3 bin/compare.py check --json`.

alerts.title: the benchmark results cannot be used
alerts.message: The benchmark results file or its trusted lines cannot be read or written: {problem}. Routing keeps the advertised scores until the file is usable.
alerts.action: check the file at the index key benchmark_results and the event log; `python3 bin/compare.py check`. See STL-MDL-753 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The benchmark results file is not valid JSON, is not a document of schema benchmarks, a row given to compare.py record is invalid, or the event log cannot take the trusted benchmark.recorded line.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/compare.py check --json`; `python3 bin/event_log.py --help`.

alerts.title: a model has no price in the pricing table
alerts.message: A call was recorded for a model that has no row in the pricing table, so its cost is not known: {problem}. It is counted as unpriced, never guessed.
alerts.action: add a dated row for the model to .stella/pricing.json (its source named), then run `python3 bin/cost.py check`. See STL-LIM-420 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The pricing table has no row for this connection and model dated on or before the call.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/cost.py check --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get pricing`.

alerts.title: the pricing table cannot be used
alerts.message: Costs cannot be computed because the pricing table is not valid: {problem}.
alerts.action: fix the row the message names in .stella/pricing.json, then run `python3 bin/cost.py check`. See STL-LIM-421 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A row breaks the pricing schema, names a connection or model the catalog does not have, or repeats a link and date.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/cost.py check --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`.

alerts.title: spans could not be exported
alerts.message: The export of call spans to the observability endpoint failed: {problem}. The spans stay in the spans file.
alerts.action: check the endpoint's host and port in its connections catalog entry, and that the receiver is running; then export again. See STL-LIM-422 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The OTLP endpoint refused, did not answer, or its key could not be read.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/stella_data.py get connections`; `python3 bin/cost.py export --spans --json`.

alerts.title: cost.py was given input it cannot use
alerts.message: A cost command could not use its input: {problem}. Nothing was priced or written.
alerts.action: fix the input the message names (a usage record needs connection, model, ts and whole-number token counts). See STL-LIM-423 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The record or option given to cost.py was malformed, or the command failed in an unexpected way.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/cost.py --help`.

alerts.title: the cost levers file cannot be used
alerts.message: The cost levers file is not valid: {problem}. Batch routing and cache policy cannot be used until it is fixed.
alerts.action: fix what the message names in .stella/levers.json, then run `python3 bin/levers.py check`. See STL-LIM-440 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The file breaks its schema, names a connection the catalog does not have, repeats a connection, lists lifetimes out of order, or holds a pattern that is no regular expression.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/levers.py check --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`.

alerts.title: a tool was removed or changed inside a session
alerts.message: A tool list for a session was refused: {problem}. A removed or changed tool would change the cached prompt prefix.
alerts.action: keep every tool of the session and add new ones at the end; start a new session to drop a tool. See STL-LIM-441 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A caller asked for a tool list that lacks, or redefines, a tool an earlier call of the session already sent.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/levers.py --help`.

alerts.title: the prompt prefix changed or holds volatile text
alerts.message: The prefix lint failed: {problem}. The provider cache would miss on this prompt.
alerts.action: remove the timestamp, run id or other changing text from the stable part (move it to a changing part), then run `python3 bin/levers.py lint-prefix` again. See STL-LIM-442 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A stable part differs from the one before it, a part was removed, a changing part comes before a stable one, or a stable part matches a volatile pattern of .stella/levers.json.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/levers.py lint-prefix PATH --json`.

alerts.title: the parallel-reviewer fan-out stopped
alerts.message: The fan-out of reviewers stopped: {problem}. No further reviewer was sent.
alerts.action: check why the first reviewer call failed or gave no first token, then send the reviews again. See STL-LIM-443 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The first call failed, or gave no first token within the wait set in .stella/levers.json.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/levers.py check --json`.

alerts.title: levers.py was given input it cannot use
alerts.message: A levers command could not use its input: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the input the message names (a job needs a kind; --by is one of card, project, role, model, connection). See STL-LIM-444 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The job, option, path or prompt file given to levers.py was malformed, or the command failed in an unexpected way.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/levers.py --help`.

alerts.title: a budget passed a soft threshold
alerts.message: A budget is getting used up: {problem}. Nothing is stopped yet.
alerts.action: look at the spending (`python3 bin/ledger.py report --by project`) and the budget in .stella/budgets.json. See STL-LIM-430 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Spending in a budget's period passed one of its soft thresholds (a percent of the cap, set in the budget).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/budget.py check --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py get budgets`.

alerts.title: a budget hit its hard cap and is on hold
alerts.message: A budget reached its hard cap: {problem}. Every call of that key is refused until you answer the approval request; with no answer it stays paused.
alerts.action: answer the approval request (approve: the budget's own option runs, a raise or a deferral to an allowed link; deny: it stays paused), or raise the cap in .stella/budgets.json. See STL-LIM-431 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Spending passed the hard cap of a budget (money or plan share).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/budget.py hold list --json`; `python3 bin/approvals.py status <request id>`.

alerts.title: a call was refused by a budget hold
alerts.message: A call was refused: {problem}. Nothing moves in that scope until the hold is answered.
alerts.action: answer the hold's approval request. See STL-LIM-432 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A hold made by a budget's hard cap is in force and has no approved answer (unanswered, denied, expired, or a deferral the data policy does not allow).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/budget.py hold list --json`.

alerts.title: a cost anomaly was found
alerts.message: Unusual spending was found: {problem}.
alerts.action: look at the card or session the message names (`python3 bin/ledger.py report --by card`); the detector settings are in .stella/budgets.json. See STL-LIM-433 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: One of the detectors (spend rate, retry loop, growing session, outlier card) matched; one alert per episode.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/budget.py anomalies --json`.

alerts.title: the budget data or state cannot be used
alerts.message: Budgets cannot be checked: {problem}. Calls that need a budget check are refused until it is fixed.
alerts.action: fix the problem the message names in .stella/budgets.json, then run `python3 bin/budget.py check-data`. See STL-LIM-434 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The budgets file or the budget state file breaks its schema or cannot be read.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/budget.py check-data --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`.

alerts.title: budget.py was given input it cannot use
alerts.message: A budget command could not use its input: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: fix the input the message names. See STL-LIM-435 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The command or its option was not valid.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/budget.py --help`.

alerts.title: the weekly model check changed a model pick
alerts.message: The weekly model check changed one model pick: {problem}. It went through the apply contract (backup, check, one event line); the command in the text reverses it.
alerts.action: nothing if the pick suits you; to reverse it run the rollback command the message gives. To stop built-in presets changing, set MODEL_CHECK_BUILTIN false with bin/settings.py. See STL-MDL-760 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: A candidate passed every rule of the check (same link class and data policy, probe record for its version, not ranking lower on the role's benchmark) and the apply tool accepted it as an engine pick.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/model_check.py status --json`; `python3 bin/stella-apply.py history role-assignments`.

alerts.title: a model pick of the weekly check was not applied
alerts.message: The weekly model check found a pick but did not apply it: {problem}. The preset is unchanged.
alerts.action: read the code in the message: usually the apply tool refused the change (STL-MDL-764) or the preset changed meanwhile; the next run tries again. See STL-MDL-761 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The apply tool refused the candidate, the owner proof was missing, or the link was changed by someone else between the check and the apply.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/model_check.py run --dry-run --json`; `python3 bin/stella-apply.py check role-assignments`.

alerts.title: the weekly model check could not check a role and paused
alerts.message: The weekly model check stopped and paused itself: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: make the model lists readable again (the connection's host, its key, the model server), then run `python3 bin/model_check.py resume` and the check again. See STL-MDL-762 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: Every link of a role that has a model list failed to give one (unreachable host, refused key, an answer that is no list), so no candidate could be judged.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/probe.py due --json` lists unreachable connections; `python3 bin/model_check.py status --json`.

alerts.title: the weekly model check is paused
alerts.message: The weekly model check did not run: {problem}.
alerts.action: find why it paused (the earlier STL-MDL-762 alert), fix it, then run `python3 bin/model_check.py resume`. See STL-MDL-763 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: An earlier run could not check a role and set the paused flag, or the check's state file cannot be read (counted as paused).
alerts.check: `python3 bin/model_check.py status --json`.

alerts.title: the apply tool refused an engine model pick
alerts.message: The apply tool refused a change offered as a weekly model check pick: {problem}. Nothing was changed.
alerts.action: nothing to do for a run of the weekly check: the next run judges again. Any other caller cannot use the engine exception; edit a custom preset instead. See STL-MDL-764 in docs/alert-codes.md.
alerts.cause: The engine exception is proved again from data under the apply lock: one model pick of one link plus one changelog entry, the same link class, reach and data policy, a probe record that meets the role, the owner setting on (built-in) or a grant in force (custom), the weekly check as caller, no --proof, no worker.
alerts.check: `python3 bin/model_check.py run --dry-run --json`; `python3 bin/stella_data.py check`.

alerts.title: a model pick could not be reversed
